data.name: Shauryaveer
data.gender_notes: Shauryaveer is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A warrior who embodies bravery and strength. Derived from the Sanskrit words 'shaurya' meaning 'bravery' and 'veer' meaning 'hero'. The name Shauryaveer carries the meaning “Brave and Mighty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shauryaveer usually hope their child will grow to embody brave and mighty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name given to one who embodies the divine qualities of bravery and strength.
data.etymology: Shauryaveer belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave and Mighty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shauryaveer total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Shauryaveer Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, a legendary king of the Maratha Empire in India, is often referred to as 'Shauryaveer' which means 'valiant' or 'brave in war'. He established the Maratha Confederacy in 1674 and made it a major power in the Indian subcontinent. His military strategies and leadership skills were instrumental in setting up a formidable resistance against the Mughals and the Portuguese, ultimately leading to the expansion of the Maratha Empire.

Another historical figure named Shauryaveer is 'Shauryaveer Chakravarti Samarth Ramdas', a 17th-century Hindu saint and social reformer. He is revered for his courage, wisdom, and spiritual guidance. Ramdas is considered the spiritual successor of the revered saint-philosopher Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and his teachings influenced the Bhakti movement in Maharashtra. He founded the city of Alandi in 1665 and built a temple there dedicated to his guru, Saint Dnyaneshwar.
